components.name: Primary Game Action
components.description: The required phase action: solid Signal Cyan, dark text, and a controlled live-state pulse.
components.css: .ds-action-primary { min-width: 200px; min-height: 48px; padding: 12px 20px; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; background: #00ffcc; color: #0a0a0f; font: 700 13px/1.2 monospace; letter-spacing: 2px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease, background 150ms ease; box-shadow: 0 0 6px 1px rgba(0,255,204,0.25), 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,255,204,0.15); } .ds-action-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 0 22px 4px rgba(0,255,204,0.45), 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,255,204,0.45); } .ds-action-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-action-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Console Button
components.description: A secondary command that stays quiet until hover or focus.
components.css: .ds-action-ghost { min-height: 44px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid #00ffcc33; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: #446655; font: 400 10px/1.2 monospace; letter-spacing: 2px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease, background 150ms ease; } .ds-action-ghost:hover { background: rgba(0,255,204,0.13); border-color: #00ffcc55; color: #00ffcc; } .ds-action-ghost:active { background: rgba(0,255,204,0.18); } .ds-action-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #00ffcc; outline-offset: 2px; color: #00ffcc; }

components.name: Segmented Choice
components.description: Mutually exclusive setup values presented as equal-width terminal cells.
components.css: .ds-choice { display: flex; width: 300px; gap: 8px; } .ds-choice button { flex: 1; min-height: 44px; padding: 6px 10px; border: 1px solid #00ffcc33; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: #446655; font: 400 13px/1 monospace; letter-spacing: 1px; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms ease; } .ds-choice button:hover { color: #00ffcc; border-color: #00ffcc66; background: #00ffcc11; } .ds-choice button.is-active { color: #00ffcc; border-color: #00ffcc; background: #00ffcc22; } .ds-choice button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Terminal Handle Field
components.description: An unboxed uppercase input with prompt glyph, cyan baseline, and terminal-cursor behavior.
components.css: .ds-handle { display: flex; align-items: center; width: 300px; min-height: 44px; border-bottom: 1px solid #00ffcc; color: #00ffcc; font-family: monospace; } .ds-handle > span { margin-right: 6px; font-size: 14px; } .ds-handle input { min-width: 0; flex: 1; padding: 8px 0; border: 0; outline: 0; background: transparent; color: #00ffcc; font: 400 14px/1.4 monospace; letter-spacing: 3px; text-transform: uppercase; caret-color: transparent; } .ds-handle i { font: 400 14px/1 monospace; animation: ds-cursor 1s step-end infinite; } .ds-handle:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 2px 0 rgba(0,255,204,0.18); } @keyframes ds-cursor { 0%,49% { opacity: 1; } 50%,100% { opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-handle i { animation: none; } }

components.name: Command Status Panel
components.description: A compact HUD module for turn state, agent identity, and cycle telemetry.
components.css: .ds-command-panel { width: 266px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid #00ffcc33; border-radius: 6px; background: rgba(5,5,15,0.88); color: #c0d0e0; font-family: monospace; } .ds-command-panel header { margin-bottom: 5px; color: #00ffcc88; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 2px; } .ds-command-panel strong { display: block; margin-bottom: 10px; color: #00ffcc; font-size: 13px; } .ds-agent { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 68px 1fr 22px; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin-top: 5px; color: #00ffcc; font-size: 9px; } .ds-agent span { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; letter-spacing: 1px; } .ds-agent i { height: 4px; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 2px; background: #00ffcc18; } .ds-agent b { display: block; width: 70%; height: 100%; background: #00ffcc; } .ds-agent em { font-style: normal; text-align: right; } .ds-agent.rival { color: #ff9955; } .ds-agent.rival i { background: #ff995518; } .ds-agent.rival b { width: 45%; background: #ff9955; }

components.name: Field Manual Tabs
components.description: Tracked uppercase navigation with an instrument-line active state.
components.css: .ds-manual-tabs { display: flex; gap: 2px; border-bottom: 1px solid #00ffcc1a; background: #05050f; } .ds-manual-tabs button { padding: 6px 12px 10px; border: 0; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; background: transparent; color: #446655; font: 400 10px/1 monospace; letter-spacing: 3px; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms ease; } .ds-manual-tabs button:hover { color: #00ffcc99; background: #00ffcc08; } .ds-manual-tabs button.is-active { color: #00ffcc; border-bottom-color: #00ffcc; background: #00ffcc0d; } .ds-manual-tabs button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Protocol Card
components.description: The playable 5:7 module with category-owned edge, circuit field, bright name, and compressed effect copy.
components.html:
SYSTEM EVENTUNCOMMON

MEMORY LEAK

Spread a slow-acting virus through a rival faction. Target loses -5 cycles.

EVT_NEG · 05
components.css: .ds-protocol-card { box-sizing: border-box; width: 150px; height: 210px; padding: 9px; overflow: hidden; border: 1.5px solid #ff3355; border-radius: 8px; background: #0d0d1f; color: #c8d8e8; font-family: monospace; transition: transform 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease; } .ds-protocol-card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px) scale(1.02); box-shadow: 0 0 18px #ff335555; } .ds-protocol-card header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; color: #ff3355; font-size: 7px; letter-spacing: 2px; } .ds-protocol-card header b { padding: 2px 4px; border: 1px solid #44aaff55; border-radius: 3px; color: #44aaff; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0; } .ds-card-art { position: relative; height: 52px; margin: 8px 0; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid #ff335533; background: #061420; } .ds-card-art::before, .ds-card-art::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 50% auto auto 50%; width: 28px; height: 28px; border: 1px solid #ff335588; transform: translate(-50%,-50%) rotate(45deg); } .ds-card-art::after { width: 8px; height: 8px; background: #ff3355; opacity: .55; } .ds-protocol-card h3 { margin: 0 0 6px; color: #ffffff; font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: 1px; } .ds-protocol-card p { margin: 0; color: #c8d8e8; font-size: 8.5px; line-height: 1.4; } .ds-protocol-card footer { margin-top: 8px; color: #4a5c6a; font-size: 7px; letter-spacing: 1px; } .ds-protocol-card:focus-within { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
Corrupt Reality is a shipboard-grade operations console still functioning while the network collapses around it. The player is an operator reading live system state, not a spectator looking at a themed card table. Near-black surfaces, Signal Cyan, compressed monospace type, framed modules, corner ticks, circuit traces, scanlines, and status language make every screen feel like one instrument.

The character is tense, technical, and decaying. Density is high but disciplined: primary actions are isolated, supporting data recedes through dim steel and terminal green, and category or state colors appear only when the rules demand them. The interface is layered rather than lifted. Tonal surfaces and hairline borders construct depth; glow and pulse are reserved for focus, selection, danger, and corruption. Glitch is an infrequent identity event, not continuous decoration.

Glossy neon arcade styling, playful pixel nostalgia, and generic dashboard polish are explicit anti-references. The system should feel purpose-built, severe, and under pressure without sacrificing the legibility required to play.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black operational canvas with thin, luminous instrumentation.
Signal Cyan owns normal player agency and live-system feedback.
Compressed monospace typography carries almost the entire interface; Doto is isolated to the game title.
Tonal layers and borders establish structure before shadow or glow.
Motion communicates boot, state change, selection, or failure; it never becomes ambient clutter.
Cards, panels, and overlays read as connected hardware modules in one failing console.

rules.name: The Signal Discipline Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan owns normal player agency; it is never sprayed across inactive content merely to make the screen feel cyberpunk.

rules.name: The Corruption Override Rule
rules.body: When corruption activates, Corruption Red becomes the environmental accent and changes the apparent operating condition of the whole interface.

rules.name: The Semantic Spectrum Rule
rules.body: Green, blue, magenta, amber, violet, and gold identify stable gameplay meanings; do not exchange them for decorative variety.

rules.name: The Doto Isolation Rule
rules.body: Doto belongs to the Corrupt Reality wordmark; operational UI stays in system monospace.

rules.name: The Compressed Transmission Rule
rules.body: Labels are short, uppercase, and tracked; longer explanations reduce tracking and increase line-height before they increase size.

rules.name: The Brightness Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Pure White and Signal Cyan are emphasis colors, not default body text; most supporting copy lives in the steel and dim-terminal range.

rules.name: The Fixed Table Rule
rules.body: Gameplay must read as one bounded table with stable anchors; do not turn primary play into a vertically scrolling page.

rules.name: The Reachability Rule
rules.body: On short or notched devices, preserve every action inside the safe viewport before preserving decorative scale or symmetry.

rules.name: The Layered-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Use tonal surfaces and borders for resting hierarchy; reserve visible glow for interaction or state change.

rules.name: The No Permanent Halo Rule
rules.body: If an element is not active, selected, dangerous, or receiving focus, it should not emit light.

rules.name: The Hardware Geometry Rule
rules.body: Every decorative line should imply circuitry, framing, calibration, or machine construction; avoid arbitrary flourishes.

rules.name: The Radius Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Controls are hardest, content containers are gently rounded, and only physical-bezel metaphors receive the largest radii.

dos: Do use Signal Cyan for normal player agency and let semantic colors take over only for their established game states.
Do keep the full table, HUD anchors, hand, and required action legible as one composition at every supported viewport.
Do preserve 44px minimum controls and 48px primary actions where React overlays receive touch input.
Do use tonal layering, thin borders, corners, meters, and calibration marks before adding glow.
Do let reduced-motion mode remove scan, pulse, unfold, glitch, and card-flight effects without hiding information.
Do keep category, rarity, rival, corruption, gain, and warning colors semantically stable.
donts: Don't turn the interface into a glossy neon arcade, playful pixel game, or generic analytics dashboard.
Don't use Doto for body copy, controls, cards, or telemetry; it is the title's signature face.
Don't make every label bright cyan or white; hierarchy depends on Dim Terminal Green and steel neutrals.
Don't use ambient glow on resting surfaces or add conventional floating-card shadows everywhere.
Don't introduce soft capsule pills, oversized rounded cards, or decorative gradients that do not describe system state.
Don't treat corruption as a local red badge; it changes the environmental accent and operating condition of the whole table.
Don't preserve decorative scale when it pushes actions outside a short, narrow, or safe-area-constrained viewport.
